My 30-year-old Kenmore dryer (wow!) was on its last legs, so I researched on line reviews and Consumer Reports. The Samsung DV56H9100GG was well-regarded, but CR listed it as #1 which sealed the deal for me. I bought mine at Home Depot and they delivered it within the week.

I've been using my new dryer for several months and it is quite a step up over the old Kenmore. It is very quiet and energy efficient. Plus there are a variety of spiffy drying options that weren't there in the old days: a "Wrinkle Prevent" to keep clothes looking good if you can't get back to the dryer in time; "Wrinkle Away" for clean stuff that just needs a spritzing and tumble dry; a variety of settings for anything from light blouses to heavy towels and bedding, and an illuminated drum so you can see what you are doing. They even include a drying rack for tennis shoes, toys, etc., though I usually just stick stuff like that out on the back porch to dry.

The Samsung dryer is several inches taller than my old Kenmore, which makes me glad I didn't buy the pedestal that raises it off the floor; I don't think it would have fit in my available space and I certainly couldn't fold stuff on the top surface. In any case, check the dimensions of your laundry area before buying.

This Samsung dryer looks O.K. (shrug, it IS basically a big box) and appears well made. It sounds cute soft musical tones and tunes to signal different features. The "load finished" tune is rather long and resembles (to me) an 8-bit version of a "Pirates of the Caribbean" drinking song. ;) The lint trap is tucked on the door edge for easy access. Unfortunately, my new dryer door opens to the right and it appears to be a tremendous hassle--possibly impossible--to change the hinge direction.

This is a pricey critter and if I ever have a problem I'll post an update immediately. I doubt I'll get 30 years like I did with my old Kenmore, but this is a really nice clothes dryer. Five stars. Lint builds up over the years in the dryer vent and can either start mucking up your drying cycle or even catch fire if it gets too hot. You should clean the duct every 2-3 years as part of your household routine.

I only have a short run of aluminum flex duct feeding to an outside wall, so it would have been just as easy to replace the duct with a new one. If you have a hard pipe that feeds up the walls, however, you really NEED this Deflector Dryer Duct Cleaning Kit or similar.

This solidly-made kit extends up to 12-feet with six soft fiberglass sections tipped with steel threads and a fat, soft brush head. You can just shove it down the duct by hand or use an electric drill to spin clean the duct with a clockwise spin. (NOTE: you MUST use clockwise--counterclockwise will unscrew the sections!) The long, soft fiberglass sections sorta flop sideways all over the place when using a drill, so you might need to slowly feed it in a section at a time. When I finished, I also used a blower to blast out the last of the lingering dust.

NOTE: Don't tear up the package it ships in--just pull out the staples. When finished you can easily repack and store the tough package on the wall.

NOTE 2: You might be able to use this kit to clean refrigerator coils. They also need to be cleaned every 2-3 years for proper operation and cooling efficiency.

This is a solid five-star cleaning kit. I've been using the Sealpod capsules for a couple of years and tried several off-brand lids to sidestep the pricey Sealpod lids. Unfortunately most off-brand lids have big issues with the adhesive or don't include that useful little side tab.

The RECAP lids worked well. The adhesive is slightly too sticky so peeling them off afterwards can occasionally prove a bit awkward. The RECAP lids do include that key side tab which helps when peeling off used lids. Mainly, however, the RECAP lids are much less expensive than Sealpod. I'll be ordering these again.

4-1/2 stars. After 15 years I had to replace my Jenn-Air glass top stove when a flashlight fell from the vent hood and broke a corner. (Grump!) I didn't want an inductance stove and Consumer Reports gave the GE JP5030SJSS 30" radiant stove high marks. I bought the stove and, of course, Amazon reduced the price $110 the next day! (Double grump.)

The stove is gorgeous and I'm glad to get rid of those pesky knobs that make cleaning the sleek stove surface awkward. The touch-sensitive surface controls four burners with a quiet musical tone when activated or changing temperature. Burners heat up FAST--about ten seconds for full blast. Lights indicate hot burners even during the cool down phase. Activating the safety lock prevents accidental touches from turning on burners.

DOWNSIDES:

The true exterior dimensions of this stove are 20-7/8 X 29-3/4. This proved a minor issue since my Jenn-Air used a slightly larger cutout.

For crying out loud, GE, include a set of wire nuts and maybe a conduit connector! They cost almost nothing. I reused my old wire nuts, but come on.

BIGGEST PROBLEM: The GE JP5030SJSS places a big honkin' box at the bottom rear of the stove, plus the overall thickness measures considerably more than my Jenn-Air or a standard coil burner stove. You are either going to have to retrofit your stove drawers or remove face plates, attach them to the cabinet and kiss off your drawers. I cut off about four inches from my drawer backs and shaved off half an inch from the top edges, but many people don't have the tools or experience for this retrofit. Be warned!

Four stars. I bought my LG LTCS20020W top-freezer refrigerator from a local Lowes, so you won't see an Amazon purchase notice. Shrug. I've only owned it for a short while, but here's the skinny:

FREEZER:

The top freezer hits the ideal 0 degrees F in just a few hours by setting the thermostat on the center position. I deliberately bought a unit with no ice maker on the theory that ice makers are notorious troublemakers. DOWNSIDE: there's NO FREEZER LIGHT. I stuck a little Motion Sensor LED Night Light to the freezer roof to fix the issue.

REFRIGERATOR:

The refrigerator achieved 37-40 degrees F in a few hours with the thermostat only on the second position. My fridge is a simple unit with LED light, two crisper drawers, a smallish dairy bin and two shelves. Some units include an optional door alarm and pantry drawer, but not mine.

OVERALL:

This LG top-freezer refrigerator is VERY quiet and energy efficient. The dimensions are excellent for my small kitchen and contains enough food for over a week for my wife and I. This refrigerator is just a tiny bit shorter and narrower than some, which can be a major plus when situating it in some kitchens, especially in older houses. But the refrigerator is an inch or two deeper than some, so measure carefully.

I didn't realize it at first, but the doors are reversible. The fridge comes set up with the doors opening to the right, but even an inexperienced person (like myself) can switch the hardware so the doors open to the left in an hour by following the on-line videos.

LG refrigerators have a some of the best reputations for reliability, so I'm expecting this LG LTCS20020 to outlast me. Five stars.

I found it very comfortable.

I wasn’t sure how I felt about the colored lights option, but I love it! You can choose red, or a brighter red, and also green and a soft lavender blue with their corresponding brighter shades. You can choose to have your color, or opt to have the unit cycle through them all. It’s quite restful. You can, of course, just use the white light. You can set the steam for a continuous output or intermittent.

The until must be cleaned after 10 hours of use. It doesn’t hold a great deal of water, so I was wondering if that was going to be inconvenient. I ran it for two continuous hours and I could tell that filling the tank twice would be about 10 hours. So THAT’S easy to keep track of!

All in all, I couldn’t be happier with this unit! It checks all the boxes and I can enjoy my essential oils in an peaceful, comforting environment. Highly recommended!! I know that loofahs take a while to break in, but I think this product has other issues. I'm a woman with smaller hands. This is just too oversized for me. It's difficult to hold and control. It's also overstuffed with a very convex surface, so only the center of the raised area actually touches my body. It doesn't mold itself to the surface of my skin, so I feel like I'm scrubbing in thin lines, and it doesn't really do the job in the dips and grooves a human body has because of that. It does dries quickly, even though I don't have anything to hang it off of. I'm pretty disappointed with this order and I can't recommend this product. I recently started using one of these with loofa on it. It works for me, even if loofa does take a while to break in. However, it also absorbs quite a bit of soap. I like this one much better.

I was a little hesitant to order it. How would silicone feel against my back? It turns out that it feels fine and works well. I like that it needs much less soap since it doesn't absorb it. Instead of spreading it all over the thing - I like the side with little bristles like a brush - all you need is to put some in the center. Moving the brush over your back spreads the soap out nicely and does the job without a lot of waste. It squeaks a bit on un-soaped skin, but that's pretty easy to get over and doesn't last long. It was just a surprise, initially. It feels like a gentle scrub, and that's the important part. It also rinses off easily and dries quickly, an important point here in our humid climate. The interior relative humidity in our house hovers around 55% in the summer, so things can get moldy fast. That's what usually happens if a loofa or any other kind of absorbent surface isn't dried properly. I just hang this up on the thoughtfully provided suction hooks and forget about it. It's great, and I'm really glad I gave this a try! This is really wonderful stuff. The application directions are unusual. I spread it gently afterwards to make sure I haven't missed any areas. The solution is very quickly absorbed and leaves my skin feeling as soft as a baby's bottom, as the old expression says. I'm mean it's reeeealy soft, and not oily or greasy at all. It's AMAZING. What really has me addicted is the smell. It's not floral or citrus, or really like anything I can put my finger on. If I had to, I'd say it's faintly sweet… possibly herbal? Well, whatever it is, it's intoxicating to me. It lingers just a while after the serum dries and I thoroughly enjoy it. I'd wear this scent as a perfume if it were available. It's not strong or offensive; it's just unique and pleasant. I recommend this with enthusiasm!! Two things drew me to ordering this product. It's a moisturizer with a scent - not something too often seen these days - but the primary aroma is definitely rose. And I just can't resist that. The scent doesn't linger and follow you around. I really only noticed it until after the cream had been absorbed. The cream itself is very sheer and feels lovely going on. It's absorbed quickly and leaves no greasy residue behind. My skin is quite sensitive and I've experienced no breakout issues. All in all, using this product has been a genuine pleasure, both tactile and sensory. This is a VERY watery product, but that's great for 2 reasons: 1) a little bit goes a long way, and 2) it absorbs really well into the skin. The best way that I have found to apply this is to tap the lotion onto my fingertips, then just sort of dab it onto my face before rubbing it in. This saves on product and keeps me from spilling any from the tube. Like I said, this has a very "wet" texture, so you won't have to use much. The price is way up there but, compared to using a lot of a cheaper product (that doesn't work as well), or a same-priced product (but using more of it), this is the best value overall. I'm going to see how long the travel-sized tube lasts while I save up for a larger size. Since this is something I have to save for, I really wish there were more size/price choices. Still, I love this and I think my skin is getting addicted to it! This works and works well. The reason I can't give it a full 5-star review is because of the price. There is a very similar product that is way cheaper and works as well or better than this one. I found Sole Magic online for about a dollar cheaper than this one. In superstores and drug stores, I found it for a couple of bucks. This one does work and I can't say one negative thing about it - other than the price. When a pedicure is around $20 (even here in Alaska where prices are high), and I can do upkeep with a similar foot smoothing pad for about $2, I just can't see paying almost $9 for this one. If other customers do want this one, I can tell you that it works, the shape is nice and makes it easy to grip and use with either hand. It's also nice that their is a coarse side and a finer side. One thing that I disagree with is that you could use this anywhere but on your feet. I don't know what would have to be going on with anyone's elbows or knees for them to use this on! All in all, a great product, but a bit overpriced when there are cheaper alternative items that are just as effective. This has the very, very *very* faintest plant-like scent (which is clean and pleasing). It's also thicker than I expected - almost like a whipped lotion. Before I used it on my hair, I rubbed some into the back of my hand to see if I'd have any kind of skin reaction. I did not. What I noticed is that once this absorbed, there was absolutely zero residue. I don't know what that means, but I was just curious. When I rub in other types of hair masks & treatments, I always get a sense of something left that I need to wash off. When I used this on my hair in the shower, I left it on for about
2 to 3 minutes after I had massaged it in according to the directions. (I have to stop and mention that I was also using the Daelong shampoo and conditioner set beforehand. That might be why I got my results.) This rinses out extremely well. My hair felt conditioned but with a lot less of the residual slip from other conditioners. That kind of worried me. I like to know that a treatment is doing something & the only way to tell until you've used it for a while is by the way your hair feels. Where I became so happy with this is an hour after rinsing it out. I have coarse and "nappy" natural African American hair. My hair tends to be extremely dry - especially after washing. A good conditioner keeps things in check until I can apply my leave-in products (oils, butters, sprays, etc.), but this time, my hair stayed soft and easy to comb through for at least 2 hours. It might have been longer, but I went ahead and applied my usual leave-ins. Still, I know that this did soften my hair (the day after, my hair is retaining softness without any more leave-in applications) without making it feel fragile. With they type of hair I have, I have to worry about breakage. I realize that I have probably been clogging up my scalp by over-doing it with the oils and butters. I like that I haven't had to use more of them for my hair to feel manageable. As a test, I'm going to try easing up on using so much leave-in stuff while I continue to use this.I think these guys are on to something here. I will have to come back and update this review as I use this for a while but, for now, I love the way this makes my hair feel, even after just one treatment. Normally, I only fully wash my hair once every four weeks or so. I will do a co-wash about every other week to keep it clean without stripping it. While I am testing this out, I plan to use it at least once a week as my co-wash. Like I said, I am also using the shampoo & conditioner of this brand. That might be a big part of why this worked so well for me, but I think that this would work just as good on its own. By the way, I'm going to alter my washing regimen for a while to use the shampoo and conditioner at least every other week. I almost forgot to mention the other thing I was concerned about: the label says that this makes the hair "straight and silky" - which is exactly what I, personally, DO NOT want. I love my texture and want to keep it. My texture is the kind that is prone to slow growth (because of breakage) so... I'm not worried about losing my naps. I'm thinking that this aids in stopping breakage more than anything.

I never knew how massive a role a filter makes in the flavor of coffee. That paired with a proper grinder makes for a very radically better cup of coffee than what I was used to. The filter is really what makes the Chemex, a Chemex. It feels sturdy, and very dense in a way. Like craft paper. It restricts water flow much better than metal filters, and I have not seen much, if any, sediment in the bottom of any of my coffee cups. The coffee comes out very smooth, and has a more refined flavor than my other ways of making coffee. The square shape of the filters threw me for a loop, but they aren't hard to use, and the box does technically show you how to open it up and place it in the pour over. Technically. Once you get your hands on it, you'll see what I mean, it's not hard, just not instantly apparent. Squares versus circles? No clue, your choice. Also, there was no paper-y flavor for me, or chemical flavor, after properly wetting the paper a good bit and pouring the water out. I will say, 20$ USD for 100 filters or .20 cents per each is not cheap at all, or even at 10$, but is well worth it. Regardless if you have a genuine chemex or some over pour over that uses pretty similar cone filters, these filters are worth your money. To review the filter is almost to review the Chemex as a whole, so rather than trying to focus purely on the filter, we have to talk about the Chemex as a whole and what the filter does. Also, quite disclaimer about this review, I have bought 200 filters in the past by buying 2 100 packs individually at different times, I bought these as I was running low, but I have NOT brewed any with this set of 200. It feels the same, looks the same, and I am certain, will act the same. So, understand I'm really just reviewing the last 200, not the next. With that out of the way, let's get into the review.

The Chemex and the filters with it are excellent tools to making good coffee. Will it make good coffee by itself? No, but it will certainly amplify a good coffee that you put in, ground in the right way with the right tools, and brewed with good technique. Is the coffee usually well bodied? Yes, but compared to a French Press with a metal filter, it isn't as thick or muddy of flavor (not a bad thing, just you don't get the underlying notes.). A Chemex makes a very well balanced cup, with alot of clarity, and it's all due to that filter. The filter is double bonded, and I won't lie, it looks like cheap napkin, but looks are deceiving.

This type comes in squares, and when you open it to put it in the Chemex itself, one side is 3 ply, the other is 1. You put the 3 ply side on the side of the Chemex with the spout to prevent airlocking so your coffee brews correctly. The Squares are actually really nice, it gives you something to grab when you are ready to throw it away. I really appreciate that, and it looks great with it. Now, you may say that the filters are very expensive, sorta. You spend $0.10 every carafe you make in just filters, but the quality of that carafe of coffee is excellent, so I never regret using a filter just to make one single cup of coffee. I will say, the drawdown time of the coffee is a little long, but that's just how the Chemex brews, and I would not recommend adjusting grind setting to change that. The Chemex just takes a little longer than a V60, but I believe the results are better to me. Overall, I think it's a brilliant way to brew coffee, and I love being able to wake up to brew a wonderful Chemex full of coffee. I like this pitcher. It looks really good, very chromed. The inside has measurement markings for each oz of milk you put in, which is a nice touch. It comes with a metal stir I think, not sure personally why it's there, but I am happy to have a stir rather than not. It's not a bad one either. The metal is reasonably thick, it's not bad quality, and steaming went well enough. I'm not the best judge of milk frothers, I don't usually use steam wands frequently, but it was pretty nice from my experience. I definitely recommend this. I have used many a coffee maker, Chemex's, Moka Pot's, French Presses, and Siphon styles. This may not be quite my favorite as the Siphon, but it is excellent. I thought when I got it "This has got to be overhyped, it's just a thick plastic-y thing!" but it really is as good as people say. Looks are deceiving. It is wonderful to use, and dead simple. Put your filter in, put the grounds in, put the water in, stir it a bit, put the plunger on, and plunge. It makes excellent coffee, very full bodied, but still with good clarity due to the paper filter. Absolutely no sediment at the bottom of the cup either! Clean up is a breeze, just take the filter holder off, and pop the filter and most of the grounds out with the plunger, rinse, and it's clean. It's so simple and easy, absolutely zero fuss! I recommend this maker for anyone wanting for a quick and easy to clean maker, or for getting into manual coffee making. It requires very little skill, but it has alot you can do, so you'll never truly master it. I bought one, and recommended it highly enough that a friend of mine did too. These filters are good, I'm not denying that. They work well, they're strong, they're bigger than you think they are, and they come unfolded. 15$ though for 100 of them is up there, because the actual name brand of this style is Chemex. These are thinner than Chemex filters, without question. They also cost the same as a Chemex filter if you buy the 200 CT of the Chemex ones, or only 3 dollars cheaper for the 100 CT. They work well in many pour overs due to their cone shape, even V60 styles of dripper. But, they are not Chemex filters and I don't believe they are worth Chemex prices.

I'm not a big believer in all the hocus pocus claims made by every single women's skin care product on the market. They all say they will make your wrinkles or crows feet shrink or smooth out or give your 40 something face a "youthful" glow again. At best, these products moisturize, cleanse, and some provide some protection from sun exposure damage.

This serum from EB5 makes the usual claims, of course, but it's not as outrageously expensive as so many of the other brands. It's a creamy concoction and it takes very little to cover my entire face - the instructions say just use one pump and that is sufficient. There's a faint scent that makes me think of Asian food - I guess that's the sesame seed oil,but the scent fades quickly. It takes about ten minutes to fully absorb into my skin, so I am not using this immediately before going to bed. I haven't had any skin irritation or breaking out in a week. Nor have I noticed any visible difference in the overall condition of my skin and no "plumping" in my laugh lines. My face is soft and it feels just a moisturized as when I use only my regular moisturizer. So....four star rating for no negative reaction and for being a nice enough moisturizer requiring very little product. This review is for the Pour Over Coffee Filter in stainless steel from Barista Warrior.

REVISED November 24, 2017 and downgraded to 3-stars.
I originally purchased this in early March, 2017. At that time I liked it very much. Over the months, it has clogged to the point where water runs through the coffee and into the Chemex so slowly as to render it useless. I've washed it carefully by hand as well as in the dishwasher and nothing seems to return it to its original, free-flowing self.

I've gone back to buying the paper filters for my Chemex and these, one-time use filters work just fine and give me a pot of coffee that doesn't have to be reheated due to the slowness of this metal filter. Recommend you do the same. Yes, I'll keep this around in case I run out of the paper filters and no, won't use it as primary any longer.

I'm very satisfied with this product and highly recommend it. An absolute nightmare to install.

Thing is, you need some additional items to install this hood (Broan 423001) and this list is neither included in the Product Description, nor the From the Manufacturer notes just below the description. However very near the bottom, beyond the point of being tired reading that stuff are the words, "BP87 dampers sold separately." Yes, it is AND YOU WILL NEED IT.

The List of What Need/Must Have To Install:
1-BP87 damper
1- 7" to 5" reducer as 5" is likely the diameter of your ducting (DO CHECK THE DIAMETER OF YOUR DUCTING). If you don't use this, return it.
1-Roll high temperature flue tape. The smallest roll I found was 5 yds long by about 2" wide. It is NOT DUCT TAPE.
The cost of these items ran about $40 more than the cost of the hood, so plan this into your cost of installing. If you don't have the correct tools such as the short list below, add still another $40 to the total cost. I got my range hood when the price dropped to around forty bucks, and with all the extras, my end cost came to just over $85.

As for tools, you'll need at least and hopefully you've got these already:
**Set of open-end wrenches (spanners for you Brits)
**3 or 4 electrical nuts to connect the fan and light wiring. Remember to GROUND THIS HOOD as spark in a grease flue can cause a fire. (most all range hoods collect grease in the filter and inside the ducting).
**Various smallish flat- and philips-head screw drivers
**A good, bright flashlight (torch for you Brits)
**Some electrical tape as you may need it. Wish I could be more specific about that.
**A great deal of patience

Some final thoughts—
Get the space where the ducting runs open and accessible BEFORE starting.
SHUT DOWN YOUR COMPUTERS AND PRINTERS then you can TURN OFF THE BREAKER supplying power to your present range hood. Household wiring is, at times, illogical and the power for the range hood could be on the same circuit as the home electronics. So shutting down your computers is a safety step to protect them from the power surge when you turn the power back on.

If the manufacturer had listed these add-on or gather together list, it would have saved me a couple hours frustration while driving around looking for the Need/Must Have stuff, it would have been much appreciated. The list under discussion is printed inside the manual that ships with the unit and while that's okay, I'd have preferred to be doing all the purchasing of these items so I could have been installing when the package arrived.

Quality:
This range hood is made with what seems to be high quality material. The finish is even on all the surfaces. Dimensions are correct and as described. The front panel switches have a solid, quality feel when turned on and off. I rated the item 3-stars for not making the list of necessary additional items clear and complete in the Notes From The Manufacturer on the page with the item's listing. These are as good as the manufacturer's variety and cost much less. Really work exactly as, or better than branded preservers we were using. This stuff isn't really widely known as carbon paper any more. I tried buying some at a local craft store and when I said, "carbon paper," got a really blank stare from the kid trying to help me. It's now more widely known as, "graphite paper," according to the kid-genius. Graphite paper sells for a much larger pile of money to purchase, and you get fewer, much smaller sheets than offered with Bestsupplier 50. As I recall, carbon is carbon and graphite is also carbon. That knowledge nugget is among the many things I don't expect anyone under 30 to comprehend, along with knowing where Australia is on a map.

Having cold drinks in my minifridge and and ice machine makes it so much easier. And, I don't dirty up the house as much, trapsing in and out.

Here are my observations about this machine:

It works by chilling the stainless steel 'tray' and running water over it. As the water gets colder it freezes in the tray. After the tray reaches a cold enough temperature, that signals the machine that the trays is full of ice. The system pauses and the ice drops into the bin. The next cycle begins.

1. I really like the way it is designed. I understand the tech inside it and am very impressed with how well it works. It is so capable, yet so compact. The fit and finish of all the components equals that of commercial machines. Very well made.

2. I like how quickly it produces ice. After I filled the tank with room temperature water, it was about 20 minutes until it dumped the first 'tray' of cubes. That load was not as well formed as the subsequent loads. But, it was good enough to ice down four tall glasses of tea. Then, it continued to pump out a new 'tray' about every 15 minutes. Each tray being better than the last. About half way through that first gallon of water, it was chilled enough that the cubes were completely formed and crystal clear.

3. I like the quantity of ice that one tank of water will produce. As you can see in one of my pictures, I have two 1 gallon storage bags full of ice, all from one tank.

4. I like the convenience. Not just about having an ice machine where I want it. But, also for the filling options. You can either fill the tank manually, and / or place up to a 2.5 gallon water jug on top for continuous operation. (The instructions really didn't go into the jug option. There is a trip plate in the ice collection bin that will stop operation, once the bin is full.

I really look forward to the warmer months, when I can be outside more, in the garage more and have cold, iced beverages on hand, thanks to this Silonn countertop ice machine.

When I use this product, it simply doesn't work nearly as well as the vinegar, so I have stopped using it. I live in a very humid state and mold growth is always a concern. It is a great adjunct to the hygrometers which are built into most dehumidifiers.

The device itself is a bright, attractive red, and the control buttons are black with easy-to-read, white labels on them. It fits comfortably in my hand. This device comes in a good quality, black, vinyl carrying case, which has a Velcro closure on the flap and a loop on the back for running a belt through it to wear it around your waist.
